title: The drain period does not end a response that is already being written.
text: `rule:concurrency/a-drain-closes-a-connection-cleanly` has the drain period bound work in progress. A request whose program is still running before it answers is cut at the period's end and answered `503` (`a_request_still_running_at_the_drain_periods_end_is_answered_503`), and the head and keep-alive waits end there (`crate::io::Phase::is_owed_nothing`). A response already being written is not: a buffered one finishes under `write_idle`, and a streamed one (`Streamed` in `serve_connection`) runs its program to its end under its own lifetime bound, so `crate::serve`'s accept loop can still park past the period. Cutting a streamed body by abandoning its peer is not enough on its own: `nvs_runtime::stream::Drain` reports a dropped producer as a clean end, so the client would read a truncated body as complete. Closing this needs the body to end in an error the connection aborts on, then the drive to abandon the peer at the period's end. `Answer`'s `Body::Error` is `Infallible`, so the request-scoped arm of `Answer::Streaming` (the one with `alive: None`) needs an error type and a period end it can read: the connection's `crate::io::DrainSeen` and the drain period, and the drive's `cut_due` cell so the loop wakes at that instant.
